name: Shree TNB Polymers
lm_rationale: Corporate Makers Capital Ltd. 2026 chittorgarh SME tracker: 8 issues managed, only 2 (25%) positive listings, 6 (75%) negative, -1.23% average listing-day gain. A weak recent record, though not the worst in the tracker.
net_proceeds: ₹15.86 Cr for capex (machinery purchase), ₹2.60 Cr for solar panel/rooftop capex, ₹1.32 Cr for PEB structure at the new manufacturing facility, ₹5.62 Cr for repayment of certain borrowings (₹25.40 Cr identified total). Balance to general corporate purposes, capped at 15% of gross proceeds or ₹10 Cr, whichever is lower.
key_risks: Top-10-customer concentration jumped sharply to 61.28% of FY26 revenue from 29.11% (FY25) and 27.04% (FY24) — no long-term customer contracts. Negative operating cash flow risk flagged (see RHP risk factor 4, though FY26 op cash flow was actually positive at ₹8.83 Cr per KPI table — company's own risk factor language references historical negative years). Manufacturing facility-II and warehouses are on leased premises. History of delayed ROC statutory filings (multiple Form 23/32 filings delayed 11-284 days, largely 2007-2010). Litigation against the company: ₹141.62 lakh (GST/tax + civil); against promoters ₹1,468.00 lakh (mostly one large civil matter).
market_moat: Two manufacturing facilities in Silvassa (23,028 sq. mtrs., 24,000 MT/year combined installed capacity) making HDPE, PP/PPH pipes & fittings, DWC pipes, sprinkler/drip-irrigation systems and industrial sheets, BIS/ISO certified, exporting to UAE, Sri Lanka, Oman and Germany. 325+ dealer/distributor network; 318 full-time employees as of 31 Mar 2026 (298 + 39 contract labourers as of 31 Jul 2026).
management: Promoters: Vijay Jaysukhlal Thosani, Rasikbhai Gokalbhai Bhalodi, Deepak Kumar Raura, Shilpaben Rasikbhai Bhalodi, Beena Vijay Thosani, Reeta Deepak Raura, Kishan Chandulal Patel, Vipul Gokalbhai Bhalodi, Hasmukhbhai Gokalbhai Bhalodi, Jignaben Vipulbhai Bhalodi and Jalpaben Hasmukhbhai Bhalodi. 45.56% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 32.76% post-issue.
prose_business: Shree TNB Polymers, incorporated 7 March 2007, is a Silvassa-based polymer manufacturer making piping systems and plastics solutions for irrigation/agriculture, potable water supply, sewerage/drainage, telecom cable protection, construction and industrial uses.
highlight_dev: Anchor round on 25 Sep 2026 raised ₹9.04 Cr from 5 anchor investors (Nexus Global Opportunities Fund, Generational Capital Breakout Fund I, IMAP India Capital Investment Trust-Catalyst New India Fund, Compact Structure, New India Vision) at ₹53/share for 17,06,000 shares (28.43% of total issue).
peer_sentence: RHP 'Basis for Offer Price' section (p.162) discloses a Comparison with Industry Peers table using CMP as of 21 Sep 2026: Shree TNB Polymers EPS ₹4.65, RoNW 13.69%, NAV ₹36.29, Revenue from Ops ₹19,812.73 lakh; Captain Pipes Ltd (P/E 40.37x, RoNW 7.15%, NAV ₹2.78), Texmo Pipes and Products Ltd (P/E 15.69x, RoNW 5.13%, NAV ₹77.19), Malpani Pipes and Fittings Ltd (P/E 7.70x, RoNW 17.65%, NAV ₹51.67). The RHP's separate 'Industry P/E Ratio' box (using the same 3 peers as its self-identified 'Peer Competitor' set) states Highest 40.37x, Lowest 7.70x — its stated 'Average' of 24/04 is a clear typo for 24.04x. At 15.87x post-issue P/E, Shree TNB Polymers sits below Captain Pipes and Texmo but above Malpani Pipes' 7.70x.
verdict_reason: steady growth and a moderate 15.87x post-issue P/E within the peer range, but a lead manager with a weak 2026 SME listing record (25% positive) and a history of delayed statutory filings
why: Revenue moved from ₹207.97 Cr in FY24 to ₹175.70 Cr in FY25 (down, on a de-growth base year) then to ₹198.31 Cr in FY26 (+12.87% YoY); PAT grew steadily FY24→FY26 from ₹5.03 Cr to ₹5.77 Cr to ₹7.13 Cr (+23.57% YoY in FY26). EBITDA margin 9.69%, PAT margin 3.60%, D/E 0.80, ROCE 16.02%, RoNW/ROE 13.69%. At the upper band, post-issue P/E is 15.87x and P/BV 1.46x — inside the RHP's own 3-peer range of 7.70x-40.37x. ₹25.40 Cr of the ₹31.80 Cr issue is identified for capex (machinery, solar, PEB structure) and debt repayment, a growth-led mix. The lead manager Corporate Makers Capital has managed 8 SME issues in 2026 with only 25% positive listings and a -1.23% average listing-day gain — a caution point for listing-day performance. Anchor book of ₹9.04 Cr was placed with 5 funds at the cap price on 25 Sep.
suggestion: Watch; the fundamentals (growing PAT, moderate leverage, in-range valuation) are reasonable for an SME issue, but the lead manager's weak 2026 listing record argues for tempering listing-day expectations rather than treating this as a subscribe-and-flip candidate.

drhp-cache/shree-tnb-polymers-anchor.pdf (Anchor Investor intimation letter to BSE dated 24 Sep 2026 board resolution; anchor bid date 25 Sep 2026; image-only PDF, OCR'd via vision)
discrepancies: RHP glossary defines 'CAP Price' as ₹52 and 'Floor Price' as ₹47 (lines 491-593 of RHP text), but the actual filed/advertised price band per chittorgarh and the anchor letter is ₹50-53 — the RHP definitions section was evidently drafted before the price band was finalized at ₹50-53 and not corrected in this copy; this card uses ₹50-53 (chittorgarh + anchor letter, both dated 24-26 Sep 2026, more current)

RHP's own 'Industry P/E Ratio' box states 'Average (Highest + Lowest /2) = 24/04' which is almost certainly a typo/OCR artifact for 24.04 (average of 40.37 and 7.70); card reports the correct arithmetic average, 24.04x

chittorgarh's KPI table shows only a single year (Mar 31, 2026) for ROE/ROCE/D-E/RoNW/PAT margin/EBITDA margin/NAV/PBV; RHP 'Basis for Offer Price' section discloses 3-year figures (FY24-FY26) for RoNW and NAV, which the card retains for FY26 only per chittorgarh's presentation convention, consistent with other cards in this ledger

RHP risk factor #4 references 'negative cash flows in the future' as a forward risk, but the RHP's own FY26 KPI table shows Operating Cash Flow of ₹883.35 lakh (positive) for FY26, ₹433.51 lakh (positive) for FY25, and ₹698.97 lakh (positive) for FY24 — all three disclosed years show positive operating cash flow; the risk factor language appears to be boilerplate/forward-looking rather than describing a historical negative-cash-flow fact, and is noted as such rather than treated as evidence of negative operating cash flow

Total Borrowing cell for FY26 (31 Mar 2026) is blank in chittorgarh's financials table; RHP KPI table does not show a separate 'Total Borrowing' line either, though D/E of 0.80 for FY26 is disclosed directly
